neighbours.label: A verb of changing a quantity or a name by a factor or into a new form (doubled, tripled, quadrupled, halved, shortened, anglicized; also 'extended the lead'), where 'to <the new value or form>' is due next; its output promotes 'becomes'/'became'
fire: Between 1950 and 2000 the city's population quadrupled to nearly two million.
Her given name, Elizabeth, was shortened to Liz when she started school.
Within five years the company's debt doubled to sixty million dollars.
The speed limit on the bridge was halved to twenty miles an hour.
A second goal extended the lead to 3-0 just before half time.
On arrival his surname, Müller, was anglicized to Miller by the clerk.
The number of students tripled to nine hundred over the decade.
The title was later abbreviated to a single word for the paperback.
quiet: Between 1950 and 2000 the city's population was counted five times by the census office.
Her given name, Elizabeth, was chosen by her grandmother before she was born.
Within five years the company's debt was repaid from the sale of two factories.
The speed limit on the bridge is enforced by cameras at both ends.
A second goal was disallowed for offside just before half time.
On arrival his surname, Müller, was written in a ledger by the clerk.
The number of students is published every autumn in the school report.
The title was later printed in gold letters on the paperback.

notes: Card: 'quadrupled to', 'shortened … to', 'name changed to', 'doubled to', 'extend the lead to'. Probes: 'shortened' 0.67, 'tripled' 0.46 (the same whether 'to' or 'in size' follows, so it fires on the verb, before the result), 'halved' 0.43, 'lead' 0.34, 'changed' 0.27; 'renamed' 0.08, 'rose to' 0.09, 'lost their lead' 0.08.
